1	# Concept — OreFlow KZ / North Pit Decision Twin
     2	
     3	**Enterprise / scope.** OreFlow KZ represents the **haulage and loading operation of a North Pit-inspired open-pit mine**. It is a source-configured *virtual* operation based on an anonymized configuration from the open-source OpenMines project, not a monitored commercial mine. Its emphasis is the operational relationship among dispatching, shovel capacity, road availability, fuel access and achievable deliveries.
     4	
     5	**Who uses it.** Mine dispatchers, shift supervisors and equipment planners who need to understand why trucks wait, whether equipment failure will impact deliveries, and which feasible assignment policy to test next.
     6	
     7	**Decision it helps make.** **Where should each available truck be sent, and what should the dispatcher change after a road or shovel failure?** Operators can compare alternatives from a common starting state, inspect queue and fuel trade-offs, and run isolated disruption/recovery forecasts.
     8	
     9	**Why this concept.** A moving truck map alone would not justify a digital twin. The value comes from equipment-linked process states, constraints and observable consequences of decisions. The existing OpenMines North Pit parameters give a transparent fleet and road configuration; Eclipse Ditto provides persisted, queryable twins rather than an animation with no platform identity. We deliberately focus on depth of haulage behavior instead of claiming unimplemented geology, blasting or processing modules.
    10	
    11	## Team
    12	
    13	- **Team 058, OreFlow KZ** — Zhenisbek Umaraliev (sole project contributor as currently reported).
    14	- **Registered GitHub login:** `jenisbekk`.
    15	- Competition repository: `https://github.com/openegiz-contest/team-058` (submit on **main**, not via this ZIP alone).
    16	
    17	## Implemented mine / what is original
    18	
    19	**Team implementation:** a continuous, event-driven North Pit simulation and monitoring/control center, source-aware truck class capacities, loading/unloading resource constraints, site queues, modeled diesel, fuel stations, scheduled maintenance, equipment state histories, policy comparisons, isolated what-if calculations, exportable operation records, a five-page spatial UI and scenario visualization.
    20	
    21	**OpenEgiz platform:** Docker-hosted Eclipse Ditto things, policies, MQTT connectivity, Telegraf, InfluxDB, Grafana and original template components. The sample mine/template does not count as team-authored work. OreFlow extends the platform with its own distinct equipment graph and behavior.
    22	
    23	**Eclipse Ditto model:** **159 defined things** in namespace `org.openegiz.oreflow`: 1 mine; 71 trucks (9 of 77 t, 29 of 35 t, 33 of 55 t); 20 shovels; 5 loading sites; 5 dumping sites; 2 fuel stations; and 55 directed road connections. Mine states and asset updates are published over MQTT and observable using the API's Ditto readback. Road topology is source-configured and drawn schematically, not real GIS routing.
    24	
    25	**End-to-end path:** OreFlow engine → MQTT → Ditto persisted twins; Ditto events → Telegraf → InfluxDB → Grafana. The OreFlow API also serves simulation-derived map frames and hypothetical branch snapshots. An operator can verify the current run with `/api/ditto/mine-01`, `/api/ditto/t001`, `/api/ditto/fuel-l0` and `/api/ditto/road-l0-d0`.
    26	
    27	## Working modules and how to see them
    28	
    29	| Module | Implemented operation | On-stand demonstration |
    30	|---|---|---|
    31	| **Haulage / dispatch** | Truck loading, loaded/empty travel, dump service, queues and Nearest/Queue-Aware/OreFlow assignments | `http://localhost:8099` → **Operations** and **Recommendations** |
    32	| **Equipment monitoring and maintenance** | Per-truck states, shovel availability, preventive maintenance/shift relief, downtime and refueling | **Fleet & Equipment** → select truck, shovel or station |
    33	| **Fuel/energy planning (modeled)** | Tank and consumption estimates, two fuel stations, station queues, fuel histories, litres-per-tonne metrics | **Operations** → fuel stations; **Reports** → modeled fuel |
    34	| **Decision support / custom module** | Compare dispatch policies, queue-relief alternatives and trade-offs via repeated deterministic simulation | **Recommendations** → analyze congestion and compare policies |
    35	| **Reports and evidence** | Hourly/daily production, truck events, shovel work, fuel, source-configuration/operation CSVs | **Reports** → choose labeled CSV export |
    36	
    37	Modules describe functions **as implemented**, not certification of real mine operations. The scenario interface can report no benefit when no tested policy helps.
    38	
    39	## What-If scenarios, demonstration and undo
    40	
    41	All scenarios in **Scenarios** are simulated in isolated branches; clicking **Calculate impact** does not alter the running mine. The comparison uses the same modeled starting conditions to calculate **Normal / Disrupted / Recovery** outcomes and presents delivery, waiting and fuel comparisons. UI scenario options include:
    42	
    43	| Scenario | Modeled consequences | How to demonstrate | How to undo |
    44	|---|---|---|---|
    45	| Shovel stops | The selected shovel becomes unavailable; queues/service/assignments and tonnes may change | **Scenarios** → **Shovel stops** → choose shovel/time/horizon → **Calculate impact** | Exit or rerun another scenario; live run never changed |
    46	| Road closes | New truck departures on the selected directed connection are restricted during the modeled outage | **Scenarios** → **Road closes** → select road → calculate; inspect road/map and deliveries | Exit or rerun; no live road closure applied |
    47	| Fuel station unavailable | Refueling availability and queue may change if the station would be used during the interval | **Scenarios** → **Fuel station** → choose L0/L3 → calculate | Exit or rerun; live station remains unchanged |
    48	| Truck failure/reduced fleet | Fewer available modeled trucks; potential throughput and queue effects | **Scenarios** → **Truck failure** → calculate | Exit or rerun; no truck disabled live |
    49	| Dump unavailable / road condition | Model-specific destination restriction or slower roads | **Scenarios** → choose corresponding card → calculate | Exit or rerun; no persistent incident |
    50	
    51	**Evidence boundary:** Road/shovel outcome calculations and scenario UI flows have been locally exercised. Some scenario combinations may have zero effect or unexpectedly increase modeled output due to rerouting or queue redistribution; not every control configuration has been individually live-verified. Recovery **production** curves are computed; there is no invented third recovery-position map where that API field is absent.
    52	
    53	## Where to see visualization
    54	
    55	Open **http://localhost:8099**. The spatial view draws model-defined loading/dumping sites, moving truck symbols, shovel identifiers, two fuel points, directed road lines, queue counts, failed-equipment indicators and incident markers. Click an asset for in-place detail rather than navigating away. **Scenarios** provides normal vs disruption map snapshots and three curves; **Reports** houses numerical charts. The visualization uses geometry inferred for a schematic display, not surveyed geographic positions. Screenshots in `presentation.pdf` come from the implemented browser client driven by recorded simulator API responses, not real mine cameras.
    56	
    57	## Data and assumptions / licenses
    58	
    59	**Source-configured data:** `team/oreflow/data/north_pit_mine.json` from [OpenMines](https://github.com/370025263/openmines), under MIT license (copy in `team/oreflow/OPENMINES_LICENSE`). It supplies truck class counts, rated capacity/speeds, shovels, loading/unloading sites and directed distance matrix. **It is not real-time telemetry and does not identify a survey-verified mine layout.**
    60	
    61	**Synthetic data:** generated truck trips, locations along schematic routes, queue minutes, shipment/production totals, diesel usage, downtime, refueling, failures and all What-If/recovery outcomes. Modeled tank capacities are equipment-class proxies; rates, slope factors, fuel pumps, maintenance, fuel price and failure processes are documented assumptions in [`team/oreflow/reports/ASSUMPTIONS_V2.md`](team/oreflow/reports/ASSUMPTIONS_V2.md). No physical sensors or ore-grade assays are connected. CSV exports carry source/simulation provenance labels.
    62	
    63	**License compatibility:** Team-authored changes are offered under MIT terms. The original OpenEgiz template preserves its `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `LICENSES/` files and bundled third-party conditions. OpenMines source is MIT-licensed. No proprietary dataset or user login is included.
    64	
    65	## Tests, reproducibility and limitations
    66	
    67	**Static/local evidence**: Authoring-environment testing covered engine and report suites, scenario isolation, twin schema cardinality, CSV schemas, server API trials, browser-fixture rendering and JS checks. After the stabilization hotfix, targeted release tests passed. These are distinct from a clean Ubuntu judge build.
    68	
    69	**User machine evidence**: The project owner ran the Docker stack and shared diagnostics where MQTT, Ditto basic readback, 71-truck model, fuel readback, Grafana and InfluxDB history succeeded. Follow-up live readbacks showed **the same run-ID** for `mine-01`, truck `t001`, two fuel stations and a road; the setup container log showed **159 registered twins**. The owner subsequently said a rerun of the full verifier was done, but **did not supply the final 16-check output in this conversation**. A fresh zero-volume Ubuntu 24.04 build is not independently confirmed here. The actual verification command is `bash scripts/oreflow-verify-ready.sh`.
    70	
    71	**Important limits:** This is a discrete-event approximation, not validated plant physics. Different policies may trade throughput for fuel; no policy is guaranteed optimal or better in a real mine. Road grades/coordinates are schematic. Some UI elements are served by simulator-derived API snapshots, while the equipment inspector verifies persisted Ditto twins; **the entire live map is not driven exclusively by Ditto reads**. Fuel/maintenance data are modeled, not field-measured. What-If scenarios are *isolated counterfactual calculations*, not destructive updates of active twins.
    72	
    73	## Submission files
    74	
    75	- `README.md` — clean VM launch and reproducible demo instructions.
    76	- `SUBMISSION.md` — this concept-first disclosure, module/scenario procedures, provenance and limits.
    77	- `presentation.pdf` — visual overview plus on-stand demonstration and source limitations.
    78	
    79	Deadline: **25 October 2026 at 23:59 Astana time (UTC+5)**. Only content committed to Team 058's **main** branch at freeze counts. Contest rules: https://openegiz-contest.github.io/kk/rules/

1	# OreFlow KZ 2.3 — Team 058 | OpenEgiz Digital Mine
     2	
     3	**North Pit: a decision-first, open-pit haulage digital twin.** This solution represents trucks, shovels, sites, fuel stations and roads using Eclipse Ditto and a continuous discrete-event simulator. It lets dispatchers observe connected equipment, compare dispatch policies, and run isolated, reversible What-If calculations.
     4	
     5	> **Data integrity:** OpenMines contributes an anonymized mine *configuration*; trips, diesel usage, truck movements, downtime, production and what-if effects are **simulated, not measured on a physical mine**. The map is a schematic based on model coordinates, not surveyed GPS.
     6	
     7	## 1. Clean installation / automated judge startup
     8	
     9	Target: **Ubuntu 24.04 amd64, Docker Engine + Compose v2**, 8 vCPU/16 GiB RAM. No preexisting volumes, passwords, cloud tokens, WSL or manual configuration are required. Run from the checked-out **repository root**:
    10	
    11	```bash
    12	bash scripts/oreflow-start.sh
    13	bash scripts/oreflow-verify-ready.sh
    14	```
    15	
    16	The startup script creates `deploy/compose/.env` locally with random credentials (git-ignored), starts MongoDB, MQTT, the five Eclipse Ditto services, InfluxDB, Grafana and Telegraf, registers policy/MQTT connections and **159 OreFlow twins**, builds the team container and runs the mine. It intentionally avoids the optional upstream Extended API Git build with an unavailable pinned reference. The readiness script polls the **real** strict integration verifier for at most eight minutes and exits nonzero if connectivity is still incomplete. Startup depends on publicly available Docker image registries.
    17	
    18	**Open on the judge VM:**
    19	- **OreFlow (main interface):** http://localhost:8099
    20	- **Grafana history dashboard:** http://localhost:3000/d/oreflow-northpit
    21	- **Ditto service:** http://localhost:8080
    22	
    23	Expected `tools/verify-oreflow.py` checks include fleet size, simulation clock, live MQTT, same-run Ditto readback, fuel and road twin state, Grafana, and telemetry history in InfluxDB. **Do not confuse a successful static Python test with a successful live-platform test.**
    24	
    25	If investigating a start failure:
    26	
    27	```bash
    28	docker compose -p oreflow58 --env-file deploy/compose/.env \
    29	  -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml -f team/oreflow/compose.yml ps
    30	python3 tools/verify-oreflow.py
    31	```
    32	
    33	Do not `docker compose down -v` unless intentionally destroying all data; it is **not** a startup step.
    34	
    35	## 2. How to demonstrate the project (5–8 minutes)
    36	
    37	1. Visit http://localhost:8099. **Operations** shows all 71 modeled trucks, five loading sites, five dump sites, 20 shovels, two fuel stations, roads, queue counts and current production. Inspect equipment on the map without leaving the page. The labels `SIMULATED MINE` and schematic-geometry notes distinguish modeled operations from measured telemetry.
    38	2. Click **Fleet & Equipment**. Open Truck `t001`, Fuel Station `L0` or a road; inspect state, modeled fuel and equipment metadata. Use the **Ditto readback** to check the platform-stored state. The live API `/api/ditto/t001`, `/api/ditto/fuel-l0`, and `/api/ditto/road-l0-d0` return current readback metadata including run-ID matching.
    39	3. In **Recommendations**, inspect current queues and compare **Nearest**, **Queue-Aware** and **OreFlow** policies on the same starting state/seed; compare delivered tonnes, waiting and modeled fuel. Recommendations are estimated trials and may show no benefit. A queue-relief action can constrain **future** assignments, not teleport trucks already queued or travelling.
    40	4. In **Scenarios** (What-If), choose **Shovel stops** or **Road closes**, select the affected asset, period and comparison horizon, then **Calculate impact**. Wait for the computed **Normal / Disrupted / Recovery** comparison, delivery curves and model-derived equipment snapshots. No incident is applied to the running mine by this button.
    41	5. In **Reports**, inspect simulated production, equipment workload, station activity and CSV exports. CSVs distinguish source-configured values from synthetic operational records and explicitly label their columns and origin.
    42	
    43	**Undo / revert What-If:** scenario calculations are isolated forecasts. Close the result or choose another scenario to return to the unchanged live Operations view. No destructive "apply outage" step is needed. For a deliberate new simulated run, choose **Start fresh mine** on Operations; it archives previous simulated history and restarts at Day 1. Browser refresh and Pause/Resume do **not** reset the mine.
    44	
    45	## 3. Architecture & project code
    46	
    47	```text
    48	OpenMines North Pit JSON -> OreFlow event engine -> MQTT -> Eclipse Ditto
    49	                                                     |      |
    50	                                                     |      +--> /api/ditto/* asset readback
    51	                                                     +--> Telegraf -> InfluxDB -> Grafana
    52	OreFlow continuous API -> spatial interface, policy trials, private What-If branches, CSV
    53	```
    54	
    55	The simulator publishes modeled equipment attributes using the OpenEgiz MQTT/Ditto pathway. The interface also uses simulator-derived API views for continuous map animation and What-If previews, and exposes explicit Ditto readback; **not every on-screen map pixel is fetched individually from Ditto**. This hybrid architecture is a known limitation, not a claim of direct physical GPS streaming.
    56	
    57	- `team/oreflow/engine.py` — source-configured, capacity/queue/fuel-constrained mine model and scenario computation.
    58	- `team/oreflow/continuous.py` — persisted ongoing mine, reports, recommendations and simulation clock.
    59	- `team/oreflow/server.py` — telemetry publisher, Ditto readback, evaluation jobs, controls and export routes.
    60	- `team/oreflow/setup_twins.py` — declares **159 twins** (1 mine, 71 trucks, 20 shovels, 5 loads, 5 dumps, 2 fuel stations and 55 directed road connections).
    61	- `team/oreflow/static/` — five-page visual UI, including enhanced road/queue/failure views and three-way scenario charts.
    62	- `team/oreflow/data/north_pit_mine.json` — original source configuration, unchanged.
    63	- `team/oreflow/reports/ASSUMPTIONS_V2.md` — detailed model and measurement assumptions.
    64	- `SUBMISSION.md` — concept, module/scenario explanations, data provenance and limitations.
    65	- `presentation.pdf` — visual presentation and on-stand demonstration.
    66	
    67	## 4. Non-Docker checks
    68	
    69	```bash
    70	python3 -m unittest discover -s team/oreflow/tests -q
    71	python3 -m compileall -q team/oreflow
    72	node --check team/oreflow/static/app.js  # if Node.js is installed
    73	bash -n scripts/oreflow-start.sh scripts/oreflow-verify-ready.sh
    74	```
    75	
    76	The full unit suite includes some computationally intensive multi-day simulations; it is not required before launching the platform. Local/browser-fixture checks and user-reported live-platform diagnostics are described in [`SUBMISSION.md`](SUBMISSION.md). **A completely clean judge-environment build has not been independently reproduced by this package author.**
    77	
    78	## 5. Provenance, licenses, limitations
    79	
    80	- Original anonymized North Pit configuration: [OpenMines](https://github.com/370025263/openmines), MIT; local copy `team/oreflow/OPENMINES_LICENSE`.
    81	- OpenEgiz template and its vendored components preserve their own notices/licenses; see `LICENSE`, `NOTICE`, `LICENSES/`.
    82	- Team-authored OreFlow changes are submitted on MIT terms as required by the contest. No personal/corporate private data is supplied.
    83	- Fuel tank classes are proxy reference values; liters/km, fuel pumps, price, shifts, maintenance, road grades and failure schedules are **assumptions**, not field measurements. The source provides **no live truck GPS or authenticated industrial sensors**.
    84	- Recovery proposals are **simulation decisions**, not validated real-mine optimization. Disruptions can produce zero or counterintuitive positive modeled production; results are not clamped to predetermined wins.
    85	- The scenario spatial comparison includes normal/disrupted states; the recovery case has a calculated production curve, but does **not** invent an unavailable recovery-position snapshot.
    86	
    87	Official contest rules: https://openegiz-contest.github.io/kk/rules/ ; judge VM: https://openegiz-contest.github.io/ru/environment/
